name: Italian Game
description: One of the oldest openings. White aims the bishop at f7, Black’s weakest square, and builds a strong center with c3 and d4.

name: Evans Gambit
description: A sharp Italian gambit: White gives up the b-pawn to gain time against the bishop on c5 and build a big center with c3 and d4.
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4

name: Ruy Lopez
description: The Spanish Game. White pressures the knight that defends e5, building long-term pressure in the center. A favorite at every level.

name: Scotch Game
description: White opens the center at once with d4, trading the e5 pawn for free piece play and a space advantage.

name: Four Knights Game
description: A classical, solid opening where both sides develop their knights first. Learn the Spanish and Scotch Four Knights ideas.
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6

name: Vienna Game
description: White develops the queen’s knight first, keeping the option of a quick f4 to attack Black’s center.

name: King’s Gambit
description: The romantic gambit: White offers the f-pawn to deflect Black’s e-pawn and open the f-file for an attack.

name: Danish Gambit
description: White sacrifices one or two pawns for a huge lead in development and two bishops raking toward Black’s king.

name: Bishop’s Opening
description: White develops the bishop to c4 straight away, keeping the knight and f-pawn flexible.

name: Ponziani Opening
description: White prepares d4 with c3, aiming for a broad pawn center. A surprise weapon with plenty of traps.

name: Against the Petrov
description: How to meet the Petrov (Russian) Defence as White, including the classical 3.Nxe5 and the sharp 3.d4.

name: Against the Philidor
description: Black defends e5 with a pawn. White grabs space with d4 and develops quickly to exploit Black’s passive setup.

name: Queen’s Gambit
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: White offers the c-pawn to pull Black’s d-pawn away from the center. Learn how to answer the Declined, the Accepted, the Slav and every other reply.

name: London System
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: A solid system: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3 and Bd3 against almost anything. Easy to learn, hard to crack.

name: London System against 1...Nf6
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: The London setup against the Indian defences, where Black often fianchettoes or hits back with ...c5.

name: Catalan Opening
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: Queen’s Gambit meets fianchetto: the bishop on g2 presses on the long diagonal and on Black’s queenside.

name: Trompowsky Attack
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: White pins or threatens to double Black’s pawns at move two, sidestepping a lot of Indian theory.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: An aggressive gambit: White gives a pawn for open lines and a fast attack on the f-file.

name: English Opening
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: White controls d5 from the flank. Flexible and strategic, often turning into a reversed Sicilian.

name: Réti Opening
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: A hypermodern opening: White attacks the center from a distance with Nf3, c4 and a kingside fianchetto.

name: King’s Indian Attack
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: A system setup with Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, d3 and often e4, playable against almost everything.

name: Bird Opening
group: Queen’s pawn and flank openings for White
description: White grabs e5 with the f-pawn, a Dutch Defence with an extra tempo. Watch out for From’s Gambit.

name: Open Sicilian
description: The main way to fight the Sicilian: Nf3 and d4, opening the center. Meet the Najdorf, Dragon, Sveshnikov, Taimanov and the rest.

name: Alapin Sicilian
description: White prepares d4 with c3 so a pawn, not a knight, recaptures on d4. A solid anti-Sicilian with a clear plan.

name: Smith-Morra Gambit
description: White gives up a pawn for rapid development and open files against the Sicilian. Full of traps at club level.

name: Closed Sicilian
description: White keeps the center closed and builds a kingside attack with g3, Bg2, f4 and Nf3.

name: French Defence
description: Black builds a solid chain with ...e6 and ...d5, then strikes at White’s center with ...c5. Learn the Advance, Exchange, Tarrasch, Winawer and more.

name: Caro-Kann Defence
description: A rock-solid defence: ...c6 and ...d5 challenge e4 while keeping the light-squared bishop free.

name: Scandinavian Defence
description: Black challenges e4 at once. After exd5 the queen recaptures, or Black gambits with ...Nf6.

name: Pirc Defence
description: A hypermodern defence: Black lets White build a center, then attacks it with pieces and a kingside fianchetto.

name: Modern Defence
description: Black fianchettoes first and keeps the knight flexible, ready to hit White’s center with ...c5 or ...e5.

name: Alekhine Defence
description: Black provokes White’s pawns forward with ...Nf6, then attacks the overextended center.

name: Sicilian Najdorf
description: The most famous Sicilian: the quiet ...a6 keeps White’s pieces off b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...e6. Learn the English Attack, 6.Bg5 and more.
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6

name: Sicilian Dragon
description: Black fianchettoes the bishop on the long diagonal, the “Dragon”. Expect opposite-side castling and races.
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6

name: Sicilian Sveshnikov
description: Black plays ...e5, accepting a hole on d5 for active piece play and the bishop pair.
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5

name: Accelerated Dragon
description: A Dragon setup without ...d6, so Black can free the position with ...d5 in one move.
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6

name: Sicilian Taimanov
description: A flexible Sicilian with ...e6 and ...Nc6, keeping options for ...a6, ...Qc7 and ...Nf6.
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6

name: Sicilian Kan
description: Black plays ...e6 and ...a6, keeping the knights home and the setup flexible.
moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6

name: Anti-Sicilians as Black
description: What to do when White avoids the Open Sicilian: the Alapin, Closed, Grand Prix, Smith-Morra and other second moves.

name: Two Knights Defence
description: Black counterattacks e4 against the Italian. Learn to survive the Fried Liver and handle 4.d3.
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6

name: Giuoco Piano as Black
description: The classical answer to the Italian: develop the bishop to c5 and meet c3 with ...Nf6.
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5

name: Berlin Defence
description: The “Berlin Wall”: a super-solid answer to the Ruy Lopez that counterattacks e4.
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6

name: Ruy Lopez Morphy Defence
description: The main line against the Ruy Lopez: ask the bishop with ...a6 and build the closed Spanish structures.
moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6

name: Petrov Defence
description: Black mirrors White and counterattacks e4. Solid and symmetrical, but beware the Stafford-like traps.

name: Scotch Game as Black
description: Take on d4 and develop quickly. Learn the Classical (...Bc5) and Mieses (...Nf6) answers.

name: Queen’s Gambit Declined
description: Black holds d5 with ...e6. Classical and solid: learn the Orthodox, Exchange, Ragozin-style and Catalan-like lines.

name: Queen’s Gambit Accepted
description: Black takes the pawn and gives it back later in exchange for free development and play against White’s center.

name: Slav Defence
description: Black supports d5 with ...c6, keeping the light-squared bishop free to come to f5 or g4.

name: Semi-Slav Defence
description: Black combines ...c6 and ...e6, a rock-solid triangle with sharp ideas like the Meran and Botvinnik.
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6

name: King’s Indian Defence
description: Black lets White build a big center, then strikes back with ...e5 or ...c5 and often attacks on the kingside.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7

name: Grünfeld Defence
description: Black hits the center with ...d5, trades knights and pressures the d4 pawn with the bishop on g7.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5

name: Nimzo-Indian Defence
description: Black pins the c3 knight to fight for e4, often giving up the bishop pair to double White’s pawns.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4

name: Queen’s Indian Defence
description: Black fianchettoes the queen’s bishop to control e4 and the long diagonal. Solid and strategic.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6

name: Bogo-Indian Defence
description: A Nimzo-Indian cousin: Black checks with the bishop to disrupt White’s development.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+

name: Dutch Defence
description: Black grabs e4 with the f-pawn and plays for a kingside attack. Learn the Leningrad, Stonewall and Classical ideas.

name: Modern Benoni
description: An unbalanced defence: Black gets a queenside majority and active pieces in return for space.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6

name: Benko Gambit
description: Black gives a pawn for long-lasting pressure on the a- and b-files.
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5

name: Budapest Gambit
description: A surprise gambit: Black hits d4 at once and usually wins the pawn back with active pieces.

name: Tarrasch Defence
description: Black accepts an isolated d-pawn in return for free, active piece play.
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5

name: Against the London
description: How to meet the London System with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6, hitting b2 and d4.
